NHS should stand for 'No Health Service'

I never thought I’d be punished for working hard — but here I am, facing financial hardship, deteriorating health, and total neglect from the NHS

Here’s what happened:

I work 12-hour days in London, with a 4-hour daily commute. That leaves me just 8 hours at home — most of which are spent sleeping. My entire life functionally operates in London, but because my home address is outside the city, my GP surgery refused to continue seeing me.

The moment I mentioned I lived out of area, they didn’t ask about my health. They didn’t ask about my symptoms, my circumstances, or my job. All they cared about was my postcode

They immediately said they’d deregister me. That was it. I was no longer a patient. No care. No options.

Now, if I want to see a GP at all, I have to travel over 70 miles — which means taking a full day off work. As a contractor, I don’t get holiday pay. I lose a full day’s income every time I need medical help. I’m now in a position where just accessing basic healthcare is pushing me toward a financial crisis.

To top it off the practice lost my test results

When I expressed distress, they told me: It is for the best you register elsewhere

I have never been rude to anyone at the practice.
